fixes.explanation: Feasts sound so respectable, so I get why this one tempts you. Still, this psalm doesn't mention them. David opens with "Blessed is the one who cares for the poor…" (Psalm 41:1). The blessing lands on someone who looks after people in need.

Right on the money. David says the LORD "…will sustain him on his bed of illness and restore him from his bed of sickness." (Psalm 41:3). Sustain and restore, those are the two things he does. I think that's a comfort to anybody who's ever been laid up.
A prayer for a son sounds like a big one, but that's not what David asks here. He prays, "O LORD, be gracious to me; heal me…" (Psalm 41:4). His ask is healing.
That's the word. The visitor "…gathers slander in his heart; he goes out and spreads it abroad." (Psalm 41:6). He takes it out the door and passes it around. Some visitors should come with a receipt.

That's the one. David says, "Even my close friend whom I trusted, the one who shared my bread, has lifted up his heel against me." (Psalm 41:9). Enemies are one thing. A friend from your own table hits different.
That's his ask. David prays, "But You, O LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up…" (Psalm 41:10). He turns to the LORD for it, which is where he went back in verse 4 too.
Hiding is a very human idea when a crowd is whispering. But David doesn't ask for it. He prays, "But You, O LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up…" (Psalm 41:10). His ask is to be raised up.

A throne would suit a king, but that's not what David says. He says to the LORD, "In my integrity You uphold me and set me in Your presence forever." (Psalm 41:12). Forever beats "many years" by a mile.

After that friend lifted his heel against him, I think David wouldn't be rushing back to that crowd. And that's not what he says anyway. He says to the LORD, "In my integrity You uphold me and set me in Your presence forever." (Psalm 41:12).

Priests are a fair guess for a psalm with a heading like this one. But the closing line says, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen." (Psalm 41:13). The blessing goes to the LORD.
